themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 137 THIS WEEK—a 474% spike vs. 23.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.39)—suggesting either a weather event, seasonal deterioration, or widespread pothole/pavement failure requiring immediate DOT response.
evidence: 137 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 23.9 weekly average (474% increase, z-score 8.39)
Street sweeping complaints also spiked: 4 last week vs. 0.4 average (967% increase)
Curb condition complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.2 average (1100% increase)
Damaged tree complaints: 8 THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 average (482% spike), suggesting storm damage may be contributing factor
reporting_angles: Interview DOT about what triggered the sudden spike—weather event, deferred maintenance, or staffing gap?
Canvass affected neighborhoods to document specific street hazards and resident safety concerns
Cross-reference with NYC Emergency Management data to see if a storm/weather event occurred THIS WEEK

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters complaints spiked 700% THIS WEEK to 11 complaints vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 9.7, highest statistical severity)—a dramatic emergence of either quality-of-life enforcement gaps, crime uptick, or community reporting shift.
evidence: 11 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 9.7—highest severity rating)
Urinating in public complaints also surged: 7 THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 average (367% increase, z-score 6.35)
Abandoned vehicles complaints up 174% last week: 36 vs. 13.1 average (z-score 5.61)
For-hire vehicle complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.2 average (1100% spike)
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and local precinct to ask what drove the spike—new enforcement initiative, crime wave, or reporting artifact?
Interview community board members and residents about perceived safety changes THIS WEEK
Investigate correlation between abandoned vehicles and non-emergency police calls—is one driving the other?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped 174% LAST WEEK to 36 complaints vs. 13.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.61)—indicating possible vehicle abandonment pattern or enforcement lag that may signal broader neighborhood blight or auto theft ring.
evidence: 36 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.1 weekly average (174% increase, z-score 5.61)
Follows non-emergency police spike this week, suggesting overlapping quality-of-life issues
311 data shows this is a sustained elevated level rather than isolated incident
reporting_angles: Map the 36 complaints geographically—are they clustered in specific neighborhoods or spread citywide?
Interview NYPD auto theft unit and Sanitation to understand if this reflects enforcement lag or genuine abandonment spike
Talk to residents and local businesses about whether they've noticed uptick in derelict vehicles and perception of neglect

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Chronic Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints remain at crisis volume with 1,504 total complaints over 90 days (highest category by far)—reflecting a structural landlord compliance failure that disproportionately affects vulnerable residents heading into winter, with no recent spike data but persistent crisis-level baseline.
evidence: 1,504 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—by far the highest complaint category (more than 3x street condition volume)
Indicates systemic landlord failure rather than anomaly; pattern consistent with prior years per CB budget requests
No recent spike data, but baseline is crisis-level heading into winter months
DOE capital projects repeatedly requested by CB suggest systemic infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Profile 3-4 families currently without adequate heat/hot water—capture human cost and health impact
Investigate landlord compliance record—use HPD data to identify repeat violators and enforcement gaps
Report on why heat/hot water complaints are so much higher in Far Rockaway vs. other districts—housing stock age, poverty concentration, landlord negligence?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Enforcement Gap
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked 1100% LAST WEEK to 3 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)—an extreme anomaly suggesting either new ride-share abuse, illegal livery operation, or sudden community reporting change requiring TLC investigation.
evidence: 3 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Extremely rare baseline (0.2 avg), making even small absolute numbers statistically extreme
Co-occurs with curb condition complaints spike (3 last week vs. 0.2 avg), suggesting possible vehicle parking/blocking issues
reporting_angles: Contact TLC (Taxi and Limousine Commission) to understand what triggered spike—illegal livery operations, Uber/Lyft abuse, or driver behavior complaints?
Review specific complaints to identify if pattern involves specific app/service or geographic cluster
Interview residents about whether they've noticed increased for-hire vehicle congestion or illegal pickups
